title.value: Approximate Planning and Learning for Partially Observed Systems
title.justification: The paper explicitly focuses on planning and learning techniques for systems where the agent has partial observability.
title.quote: In this talk, we describe a new framework for approximate planning and learning for partially observed systems.

analysis.description: This paper presents a novel framework for reinforcement learning in environments where the agent has partial observations of the state. It builds upon existing theories of Markov decision processes and introduces the concept of approximate information state to enhance the planning and learning capabilities of agents.

type.justification: The paper primarily discusses a new theoretical framework and provides insights into the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning in partially observed environments.
type.quote: The talk will highlight the strong theoretical foundations of this framework, illustrate how many of the existing approximation results can be viewed as a special case of approximate information state.

name.justification: The research paper focuses on developing a framework for reinforcement learning under partial observability.
name.quote: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a conceptual framework for designing agents which learn to act optimally in an unknown environment.

name.justification: The paper introduces a framework specifically for systems with partial observability, enhancing existing reinforcement learning methods.
name.quote: In various applications including robotics, finance, and healthcare, the agent only gets a partial observation of the state of the environment.

name.justification: The paper draws on the theory of Markov decision processes to develop its new framework for reinforcement learning.
name.quote: The success of RL is based on a solid foundation of combining the theory of exact and approximate Markov decision processes (MDPs)...
